docs.text:
Batch results/df/dftwo_counts_area_20261013, refitted after the count-likelihood correction. All four valid starts reach the same minimum (objectives within 0.01); numerical validation passes; no parameter sits at a bound.

Quantity 2026-10-13 (current) 2026-09-23 (superseded) \(\chi^2_{\rm kin}\) (89 bins) 156.4 (1.76 per bin) 158.1 (1.78) HST count deviance (20 bins) 96.9 98.9 Gaia count deviance (12 bins) 25.2 26.3 \(M_\star\) (best fit) 3.00×10⁶ M☉ 3.00×10⁶ M☉ \(M_{\rm rem}\), \(a_{\rm rem}\) 2.73×10⁵ M☉, 2.18 pc 2.62×10⁵ M☉, 2.15 pc Distance 5.356 kpc 5.356 kpc Mass per F625W < 19 star 10.48 M☉ 10.67 M☉ Data-fit gate fails fails

Star counts, MUSE line-of-sight and HST/Gaia proper-motion dispersions against the current (blue) and superseded (orange) fits; dashed: the earlier Jeans model. Bottom row: residuals (signed Poisson deviance residuals for the counts). Both fits are evaluated with the corrected count likelihood.

The two count profiles do not join, by design: they are different selections in their own units. HST counts are oMEGACat stars with F625W < 19 at 2–250″; Gaia counts are stars with G < 17 at 300–2400″. The brighter Gaia limit counts fewer stars per unit stellar mass (fitted amplitude ratio 13.7 with free amplitudes and raw counts; measured 11.42 ± 0.23 for complete samples, i.e. 11.95 ± 0.3 expected for the raw counts; count-ratio check), so each profile has its own fitted count amplitude (aHST, aGaia), and the Gaia model also includes a uniform field of about 1.6 stars arcmin⁻². The model curves are the same stellar surface density scaled by each amplitude. The gap between 250″ and 300″ is a gap in coverage.

docs.title: Comparison with the Jeans model (dashed curves)
docs.text:
Full description, figures and posterior: Jeans comparison model.

The dashed curves are the best rung-2 spherical Jeans fit without dark matter (results/fits/rung2_K1_turnover, J-Trager), the best no-DM model of the earlier Jeans ladder. Both models are fitted to the same 89-bin kinematic snapshot, so their kinematic χ² compare directly; the Jeans fit uses a fixed light profile (an MGE of the Trager+1995 profile joined to HST star counts) instead of the Poisson star counts.

Jeans (rung 2, no DM) DF base model Stellar tracer and mass MGE light profile, mass-to-light free self-consistent action DF Free stellar parameters \(M_\star\) only (density shape fixed by the light) \(M_\star\) and six DF parameters (shape fitted to the counts) Anisotropy turnover β(r): β₀ = −0.50 (centre) → +0.20 → −0.98 (outside) isotropic core → +0.15 near 8 pc → −0.53 at 100 pc Central black hole 4.41×10⁴ M☉ (ML); 4.25 (3.92–4.58)×10⁴ (median, 16–84%) none \(M_\star\) 2.37×10⁶ M☉ (ML) 3.00×10⁶ M☉ (best fit) Remnants (Plummer) 7.7×10⁵ M☉, a = 5.7 pc (ML) 2.7×10⁵ M☉, a = 2.2 pc (best fit) Total mass, M★ + Mrem + MBH 3.18×10⁶ M☉ (ML); 3.24×10⁶ (median) 3.27×10⁶ M☉ (best fit) \(M_\star/L_V\), \(M_{\rm tot}/L_V\) 2.0, 2.7 (ML); 2.3, 2.8 (median) 2.6, 2.8 Distance 5.34 kpc 5.36 kpc χ² (per bin) Jeans DF HST PM radial (21) 61.8 (2.94) 42.6 (2.03) HST PM tangential (21) 36.6 (1.74) 39.8 (1.89) MUSE LOS (29) 51.7 (1.78) 38.1 (1.31) Gaia PM radial (9) 16.9 (1.88) 14.4 (1.60) Gaia PM tangential (9) 23.0 (2.56) 21.5 (2.39) Total (89) 190.0 156.4
  • The DF fits better than J-Trager overall (Δχ² = 34) and in every dataset except the HST tangential proper motions. This holds for the light-profile tracer only: the Jeans twin with the star-count tracer (J-counts) reaches χ² = 152.2 (ML), below the DF's 156.4, with M_BH = 3.67 (3.30–4.02)×10⁴ M☉ (posterior median) and M_rem = 8.4×10⁵ M☉.
  • The Jeans model follows the central rise of the HST proper-motion dispersions inside 0.3 pc (~11″), which the DF, with an isotropic core and no black hole, stays below by 1.5–2.4σ in several bins: χ² = 7.3 (Jeans) against 21.5 (DF) for those 10 bins. This is where the black hole matters.
  • It pays for this at intermediate radii: at 2–20 pc (36 bins of HST, MUSE and Gaia) χ² = 122.2 (Jeans) against 77.8 (DF), mostly in the HST radial proper motions (40.2 against 20.2) and the MUSE line-of-sight dispersions (30.9 against 18.7).
  • The black hole is tied to an imposed anisotropy. A cored stellar density around a point mass needs β₀ ≤ −½ for any non-negative DF; the prior enforces it and the fit sits at the bound (β₀ = −0.503). Even so, under the standard separable construction a non-negative DF fails to exist at 0.02–0.18 pc, where the black hole dominates (89.7% of posterior draws fail; no failure outside ~0.2 pc; a non-separable DF is not excluded; DF consistency audit). The DF base model is non-negative by construction.
  • Both put about the same total mass in the cluster (3.2–3.3×10⁶ M☉) but divide it differently: the Jeans fit has 20% less stellar mass and nearly three times more remnant mass, spread over a 2.5× larger scale. This is the same stars-versus-dark-mass degeneracy seen within the DF fits.
  • Why \(M_\star\) differs by 11% at the same total mass. In neither model is the stellar mass fixed by the light or the counts; it is the normalisation the kinematics leave after the remnants (and, for Jeans, the black hole and the imposed central anisotropy) take their share. The remnant mass is close to the total minus \(M_\star\), so with remnants at 8–17% of the total, a 1% change in \(M_\star\) moves \(M_{\rm rem}\) by ~10%.
  • A central black hole in the DF (DF + central black hole, 2026-10-15, fixed masses, 2026-10-13 count likelihood): 8,200 M☉ lowers the objective by 5.5; 4×10⁴ M☉ lowers χ²_kin by 12 but loses 15 in the HST counts, because its cusp over-predicts the central counts. The differences are not calibrated with mocks. Whether the inner rise needs a black hole, radially biased central orbits or mass segregation is not settled.

docs.text:
Current fit, by component. (a) Density; (b) enclosed mass with the half-mass radii dotted; (c) circular velocity; (d) remnant share, local (\(\rho_{\rm rem}/\rho_{\rm tot}\)) and cumulative (\(M_{\rm rem}/M_{\rm tot}\)); (e) dynamical-to-stellar mass ratio.   • Two components with different scales. The stars have a 3D half-mass radius of 10.4 pc (projected 7.7 pc; the Baumgardt database lists r_h = 7.56 pc at 5.43 kpc, i.e. 7.46 pc at the fitted distance); the remnant Plummer has 2.8 pc.

  • Circular velocity peaks at 27.0 km/s at 9.0 pc; the stars alone peak at ~25 km/s near 10 pc, the remnants at ~14 km/s near 3 pc. The central escape speed is 68 km/s.
  • The total inside 10 pc differs from the superseded fit by −0.7%.
  • The remnant component matches published fits. Its best-fit mass and scale (2.73×10⁵ M☉, 2.18 pc; the tied refit gives 2.00×10⁵ M☉, 1.88 pc) agree with the extended central mass of Bañares-Hernández+2025 (2.65×10⁵ M☉ in a 1.88 pc Plummer); black-hole-only estimates are 1.35–1.82×10⁵ M☉. See Remnant mass and spatial scale.

docs.title: Internal kinematics
docs.text:
(a) Intrinsic radial and tangential (one component) dispersions, with the local escape speed/√12 for scale; (b) anisotropy β(r); (c) stellar surface density with the projected and 3D half-mass radii; (d) projected line-of-sight and proper-motion dispersions from the DF, before the published rotation is subtracted in the likelihood.

  • Isotropic core, radial bias at intermediate radii, tangential outskirts. β = 0.00 at 0.3 pc, 0.09 at 3 pc, peaks at +0.15 near 8 pc, crosses zero near 22 pc, and reaches −0.08 at 30 pc and −0.53 at 100 pc.
  • Central dispersion σ_r ≈ σ_t ≈ 21.4 km/s; σ_r = 14.7 and σ_t = 13.5 km/s at 10 pc.
  • Projected dispersions in the core: 19.8 km/s along the line of sight and 19.3 km/s in each proper-motion component. The radial and tangential proper-motion profiles differ by ≲ 0.5 km/s inside 30 pc and separate in the tangentially biased outskirts.

docs.title: Distribution function
docs.text:
(a) Intrinsic moments and β(r); (b) the anisotropy bias \(b(q)\), \(q=J_r+L\), over the action distributions of the stars in the HST/MUSE (R ≤ 9.5 pc) and Gaia (9.4–63 pc) ranges, with the two transitions \(J_a\) and \(J_{\rm outer}\) dotted; (c) \(f(J_r, L)\).

  • The radial bias (b ≈ +0.45 at its peak) sits on the actions of the HST/MUSE stars; the tangential tail (b → −0.33) sits on the Gaia stars. The data constrain the DF over \(q\) ≈ 10–1000 pc km/s; outside that range its shape is extrapolated.
  • \(f\) is smooth and monotonic in both actions, with no features at the transitions.

docs.title: What the base fits establish
docs.text:
• No dark matter is needed to fit the kinematics and counts. A free cored halo goes to \(\rho_{20}=0\), with the old count likelihood (2026-09-23) and again with the tied, completeness-corrected counts (2026-10-16); the Jeans fits show no preference for a halo either (dark-matter fits).
  • The total mass profile is constrained; its split is not. Mocks drawn from the base model recover the total mass to ±3% at 20 pc and ±5% over 2–40 pc, but stars trade against remnants plus halo through the count amplitude, and the recovered \(\rho_{20}\) scatters by ±0.7 M☉ pc⁻³.
  • The answer depends on the stellar mass per counted star. Fixed at the photometric 8–9 M☉ per F625W < 19 star, the data prefer \(\rho_{20}\) ≈ 2–4; at the dynamical value (now 10.5) they prefer none. The photometric estimate (8.3–9.8 in the zones that dominate the kinematics) is not precise enough (~1 M☉ per star; ~0.3 is needed) to decide.
  • The fit is not statistically acceptable. χ²_kin per bin is 1.76 against the gate of 1.3, and the HST count residuals are structured: data below the model near 1 pc and in the outermost HST bin (~6 pc), above it at 3–4 pc. Either the error bars are underestimated or the model lacks freedom (mass segregation, rotation, a different remnant shape); this is not yet separated.

docs.title: Dark-matter survival and tidal tails
docs.text:
• Restricted and live N-body runs of a no-DM and a DM model on Omega Cen's orbit (static McMillan17, 1.96 Gyr) give tails whose kinematics agree to 10%. The DM model loses 1.3–1.6× fewer stars. Neither difference is testable with the published tail data (Kuzma+2021, 2021MNRAS.507.1127K; Kuzma+2026, 2026MNRAS.550g1147K; Ibata+2019, 2019NatAs...3..667I).
  • Fitted halos are compact (r_s at the 5 pc bound) and traded against stellar mass, so across the kinematically allowed range the Jacobi radius at pericentre changes by ≤ 6.5%. Dark matter that could affect the tails lies beyond ~80–200 pc and is not constrained by the kinematics.

Reports: dynamical experiments, first batch (PDF), batch analysis, progenitor orbits, Section-11 tests, lifetime evolution (paused), DM capture constraints (PDF), N-body code assessment, N-body ICs.

docs.title: Key facts
docs.text:
• Reference inputs. The reference DF fit is results/df/dftwo_counts_area_20261013 (best job observed_no_halo_start3; base model). It uses:
  • five kinematic profiles: hst_pm_radial_ours, hst_pm_tangential_ours, muse_los_dispersion, gaia_edr3_ours_radial, gaia_edr3_ours_tangential (89 bins in total);
  • two Poisson count profiles, schema 2 (area-weighted covered-area quadrature, commit 1af8c33): ocen_counts_hst_f625w19 (20 bins) and ocen_counts_gaia_g17 (12 bins).

The kinematics are frozen in observed/data_snapshot.json (sha256 570399f3…). That snapshot was copied from results/df/pilot_no_dm_20260922, which took it from the Jeans run results/fits/rung2_K1_turnover. The rung-1 and rung-2 Jeans ladder runs carry the identical snapshot sha. - Tied variant. results/df/dftie_restart_20261016 uses the same kinematic snapshot with the completeness-corrected counts ocen_counts_hst_f625w19_c and ocen_counts_gaia_g17_c and the amplitude tie ocen_counts_tie_c.json (driver option --count-tie). Its halo test is results/df/dftie_halo_20261016. - Products reproduce the reference fits. On 2026-10-13 I reloaded the five profiles through ocen_dm.kinematics.likelihood.load_profile. Values and errors match the frozen snapshot exactly (max |Δ|/σ = 0), although ocen_pm_dispersion_edr3_ours.ecsv was rebuilt on 2026-10-11. The sha256 of the current proc/kinematics/ocen_counts_*.json and *_c.json files match those recorded in the two runs' problem.json (checked 2026-10-17). - Historical count products. results/df/dftwo_counts_20260923 (the previous baseline) and the rho20scan_*, mpsscan_* and mock runs of 2026-09-23 used schema-1 count files (star-weighted quantile nodes, biased). Their sha256 values match proc/kinematics/ocen_counts_*_schema1_20260923.json. These runs have not been redone with schema 2. - Indirect inputs. Several products feed the reference fit without being likelihood terms themselves:

Product How it reaches the reference fit Vasiliev & Baumgardt (2021) PM profiles PM rotation curve used for the tangential streaming subtraction and its error oMEGACat LOS rotation MUSE streaming term Gaia DR3 field template from WSDB Used by both of our own PM-dispersion builders Composite tracer profile (Trager 1995 plus oMEGACat selection_hq_f625w star counts) Gaia depth-dispersion correction Vasiliev & Baumgardt member catalogue Parent sample for the Gaia PMs and the Gaia counts oMEGACat star catalogue Parent sample for the HST PMs and the HST counts
  • Main gaps. Detailed in Section 3:
  • The registry (provenance/datasets.yaml) covers only the September kinematics/tails datasets. All stream-project inputs are registered only in configs/data.yaml or the project journal, or not at all: STREAMFINDER 2021/2024, HST LP, the Tango Zenodo archive, Hunter+2024 potentials, gc_catalog_full.fits and Gaia XP pulls.
  • One of them, the HST LP fields (S9), now sets the Gaia count completeness used in the tied DF and J-counts fits, so an unregistered input enters a likelihood.
  • Several WSDB caches that every stream fit depends on have no builder script.
  • manifest.json and checksums.txt contain stale entries.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
All drawn from the current processed products (bin/plot_data_products.py, ocen plot-data, bin/build_mass_function.py).

The 89 kinematic bins of the reference fit (colour) and published profiles that are not fitted. Top: HST proper-motion dispersions, radial and tangential (ours, black; oMEGACat VI published, grey) continued outward by our Gaia EDR3 profiles (blue); dashed: the rotation term each fitted profile carries. Bottom left: MUSE line-of-sight dispersion with its rotation term (v_rot/√2). Bottom right: published one-dimensional Gaia proper-motion profiles (Vasiliev & Baumgardt 2021, Baumgardt+2019) against ours; the Vasiliev & Baumgardt profile lies below the HST values inside ~200″. Proper motions in mas/yr (right axis: km/s at 5.43 kpc).

Rotation used in the streaming correction. Left: Vasiliev & Baumgardt 2021 proper-motion rotation curve (median, 16–84% and 2–98%), peaking at 0.25 mas/yr (≈6.4 km/s) near 450″. Right: MUSE line-of-sight rotation amplitude (oMEGACat VI), rising from ~3 to ~7 km/s between 30″ and 300″.

The Poisson star-count products. Left: surface number density, HST F625W < 19 (2–250″, 117,751 stars) and Gaia G < 17 (300–2400″, 18,289 stars including field). Middle: stars per bin. Right: covered fraction of each annulus (≥ 0.995).

The published oMEGACat VI profiles: proper-motion dispersions (combined, radial, tangential), the σ_R/σ_T anisotropy diagnostic (isotropic inside ~100″, radially biased outside), MUSE line-of-sight dispersion and rotation.

Three-dimensional kinematics of the core from the same stars: line-of-sight velocity field with the fitted rotation axis; plane-of-sky versus line-of-sight rotation; the three velocity components; and proper-motion against line-of-sight dispersions, which agree at the adopted distance.

Shape of the light profile: the MGE of the Trager+1995 profile (used as the tracer of the earlier Jeans fits) against star counts from HST oMEGACat, Gaia EDR3 members and Gaia+Pristine members, each anchored where complete. Beyond the Trager data the MGE is an extrapolation.

oMEGACat colour–magnitude diagram, 30–250″, all stars (left) and with both quality flags (right). Dotted: F625W = 18 (turnoff), 19 (count-product limit) and 23 (luminosity-function turnover).

Present-day mass function from the unflagged oMEGACat sample with a MIST 12.5 Gyr isochrone: CMD and ridge line; luminosity functions in five radial zones; mass functions over 0.52–0.78 M☉ with slopes steepening outward (−1.37 to −1.77); the light-following mass per F625W < 19 star for each variant; and the budget in the 60–100″ zone (observed main sequence, extrapolation below 0.52 M☉, evolved stars, white dwarfs).

docs.title: 0. How the reference DF likelihood consumes its data
docs.text:
• Driver. bin/run_compact_df_recovery.py.
  • prepare-real (prepare_real, lines 228–330) copies proc/kinematics/<count>.json into the run directory and records each sha256 (lines 254–257).
  • It copies the kinematic data_snapshot.json from results/df/pilot_no_dm_20260922; --start-from sets the starting configuration.
  • With --count-tie JSON (line 829) it stores the amplitude tie in problem.json and the batch manifest.
  • It writes problem.json. The reference record is photometry: false, counts: [ocen_counts_hst_f625w19, ocen_counts_gaia_g17].
  • At run time load_problem (lines 62–74) verifies the count sha256 and rebuilds the DFJointProblem, with the tie if one is recorded.
  • Frozen inputs of the reference fit, results/df/dftwo_counts_area_20261013/observed/:
File Size (B) data_snapshot.json 19,656 ocen_counts_gaia_g17.json 5,368 ocen_counts_hst_f625w19.json 9,132 problem.json 740

batch.json records source_commit 1af8c33, gaia_error_floor_masyr 0.0 and distance 5.43 (fixed in the starting config; free between 4.8 and 6.0 in coordinates; the same in the tied variant). The count files are schema 2, and their sha256 match the current products. - Tied variant. results/df/dftie_restart_20261016/observed/ holds the same data_snapshot.json, ocen_counts_hst_f625w19_c.json (12,016 B), ocen_counts_gaia_g17_c.json (7,444 B) and a problem.json (1,085 B) that carries the count_tie record (ratio 11.4162 ± 0.2273). batch.json records source_commit 30bdcb3. - Snapshot chain. The data_snapshot comes from results/df/pilot_no_dm_20260922, whose run.json has data_source = results/fits/rung2_K1_turnover. The sha256 570399f38ab2… is identical in rung1_K1_slice/summary.json and rung2_K1_turnover/summary.json. - Gate output. report.json lists χ² per point by dataset and the count deviance, for the best job of each fit:

Dataset χ²/pt, reference (start 3) χ²/pt, tied (start 0) hst_pm_radial_ours 2.03 2.09 hst_pm_tangential_ours 1.89 2.02 muse_los_dispersion 1.31 1.33 gaia_edr3_ours_radial 1.60 2.12 gaia_edr3_ours_tangential 2.39 1.69 HST counts, deviance / bin 4.85 4.21 Gaia counts, deviance / bin 2.10 3.82

The tied fit's amplitude ratio is 11.88 against the prior 11.42 ± 0.23 (χ² 4.2). - Historical baseline. results/df/dftwo_counts_20260923 (schema-1 counts, source_commit 36bca6f) was the baseline until 2026-10-13. Its frozen count files (3,226 and 5,411 B) match proc/kinematics/ocen_counts_*_schema1_20260923.json; its start-0 deviance per bin was 4.94 (HST) and 2.19 (Gaia). - Default dataset list. src/ocen_dm/cli.py:364 DEFAULT_DATASETS holds the same five kinematic keys. - The note at cli.py:359–363 records why gaia_edr3_pm (published VB21 spline) was replaced on 2026-09-19. - It also records why gaia_dr2_pm was dropped on 2026-09-20. - Duplicate guard. likelihood.py:373 _FORBIDDEN_TOGETHER refuses combinations that share stars, for example published plus "ours" HST, or VB21 plus our Gaia.

docs.title: K1. HST PM dispersion, our measurement (hst_pm_radial_ours, hst_pm_tangential_ours)
docs.text:
• Source. oMEGACat VI (Häberle et al. 2025, ApJ).
  • arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.04903
  • DOI: https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-4357/adbe67
  • Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14978551
  • Raw file. raw/omegacat_vi_kinematics/catalog_and_selections.fits (260,994,240 B). The published md5 9de5a701… was verified in provenance/manifest.json. Since 2026-10-16 data/raw/omegacat_vi_kinematics may be a local link to an external copy of the release; the files were re-verified against provenance/checksums.txt after the move.
  • Builder. src/ocen_dm/kinematics/hst_profile.py:
  • load_hst_sample (:112)
  • hst_profile (:170)
  • build_hst_profile (:221, writes :243)
  • load_hst_product (:248)
  • Selection.
  • oMEGACat selection_hq_astrometry > 0 (flagged stars only; require_flag=True, correct_unflagged=False).
  • Edges DEFAULT_EDGES = geomspace(2, 250, 21) ∪ [300, 340, 360] arcsec (:101), giving 21 bins (r_median 3.65–341.5″).
  • Each bin is fitted as a cluster 2-D Gaussian plus a field mixture, using the K8 field template in absolute PM.
  • Product. proc/kinematics/ocen_pm_dispersion_hst_ours.ecsv (10,949 B; built 2026-09-20T08:46Z).
  • Columns: r_lower/r_median/r_upper [arcsec], n_stars, n_flagged, f_unflagged, f_field, sigma_pmr(_err), sigma_pmt(_err), sigma_pm(_err) [mas/yr], sigma_raw, sigma_sys, sigma_kms(_err), r_pc, r_node0..7.
  • Metadata: unflagged_bias (1.077, 0.011) is recorded but not applied.
  • Likelihood use. likelihood.py:275 _hst_ours.
  • Errors are symmetric.
  • The tangential component adds ⟨μ_T⟩² from the K5 rotation curve as streaming2. The rotation-curve error is propagated in quadrature (streaming_error_on_sigma, :153).
  • r_nodes gives star-weighted radial averaging.
  • Restrictions.
  • Metadata note: HST PMs are locally corrected, so the dispersion is about a rotation-free mean.
  • Shares stars with K7, so the two cannot be combined (_FORBIDDEN_TOGETHER).
  • Status. a, b (Jeans rung0/1/2). The loader auto-builds the product if it is missing, per the README.

docs.title: K2/K3. MUSE LOS dispersion and LOS rotation
docs.text:
• Source. oMEGACat VI, as for K1.
  • Raw file. raw/omegacat_vi_kinematics/los_profile.fits (17,280 B; md5 verified). The .dat twin (4,237 B) is unused.
  • Builder. src/ocen_dm/data/omegacat.py:257 preprocess (CLI ocen preprocess --dataset omegacat, cli.py:82). The configuration is in configs/data.yaml omegacat_vi.products.
  • Products.
  • proc/kinematics/omegacat_vi_los_dispersion.ecsv (29 rows). r_median 5.66–290.3″ (edges 0–332.3″). Columns sigma_los, sigma_los_err_lo/hi [km/s], plus src_* copies.
  • proc/kinematics/omegacat_vi_los_rotation.ecsv (29 rows). Columns v_rot, v_rot_err_lo/hi [km/s], theta_0 [deg].
  • Likelihood use. likelihood.py:172–203.
  • The two-piece Gaussian handles the asymmetric errors.
  • streaming2 = v_rot²/2 (:182–186), with a check that the bins are identical.
  • No rotation error is propagated for MUSE (module docstring).
  • Metadata rule (ocen_likelihood_rule): "binned profile: compare a model integrated over the same radial bin and tracer selection; bins share stars with other binnings of the same data, so alternative binnings are not independent likelihood factors".
  • Status. a, b.

docs.title: K4. Gaia EDR3 PM dispersion, our measurement (gaia_edr3_ours_radial, gaia_edr3_ours_tangential)
docs.text:
• Source. Vasiliev & Baumgardt (2021), MNRAS 505, 5978.

  • DOI: https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stab1475

docs.title: Ratio of the two count products in the overlap (2026-10-16)
docs.text:
The fits give C1 and C2 separate free amplitudes, aHST and aGaia. For a single cluster with a single stellar population, their ratio N(F625W < 19)/N(G < 17) is set by the luminosity function. So it can be measured where both catalogues are complete and compared with the fit. The amplitudes have not been tied, and nothing was refitted.

(a) Completeness against radius.

  • Gaia: the fraction of bright HST stars (F625W < 16.5) with a Gaia counterpart. The match uses a 0.06″ tolerance, after removing the (−0.045, −0.090)″ offset between the two catalogue epochs.
  • HST: the fraction of oMEGACat stars with a measured F625W.

(b) N(F625W < 19)/N(G < 17), from both catalogues counted in the same area (the 3″ cells holding oMEGACat stars), with the 1.60 arcmin⁻² Gaia field subtracted.

  • Black and grey points: the ratio in 25″ annuli.
  • Orange: the 250–300″ annulus.
  • Green: HST alone, N(F625W < 19)/N(F625W < 16.83). Here 16.83 = 17 + (F625W − G), with F625W − G = −0.171 the median for matched stars at 16.5 < G < 17.5.
  • Purple lines: the fitted aHST/aGaia.*

Script: bin/check_count_ratio_overlap.py. Numbers: results/plot_data/count_ratio_overlap.json.

Where the measurement is possible.

  • Inside 250″ Gaia is incomplete. It recovers 18 % of bright HST stars at 50–75″ and 84 % at 225–250″. The direct ratio therefore climbs inwards (grey points).
  • Beyond 300″ HST is incomplete. The mosaic edge leaves only 67 % and 23 % of stars with F625W at 300–325″ and 325–350″.
  • Both catalogues exceed 0.9 completeness only at 250–300″. Even there Gaia is 0.91–0.92 complete, not 1.

Results.

Estimate N(F625W<19)/N(G<17) Direct, 250–275″ (Gaia 0.92, HST 0.98 complete) 13.2 ± 0.5 Direct, 275–300″ (Gaia 0.91, HST 0.92 complete) 11.4 ± 0.5 Direct, 250–300″ 12.40 ± 0.34 HST alone: ratio for a complete G < 17 sample, 50–300″ 10.3–11.6, no radial trend HST alone, divided by the measured Gaia completeness at 250–300″ ≈ 12.3 Fitted aHST/aGaia: no BH, BH 8,200, BH 4×10⁴ 13.72, 13.70, 13.49
  • The fitted amplitudes include Gaia's incompleteness. A completeness factor below 1 lowers aGaia and raises the fitted ratio. So the fit should be compared with the raw ratio of Gaia's counts, not with the HST-alone ratio.
  • Against the directly measured ratio, the fit is high by 0–10 %.
    • It is high by 4 % (1σ) at 250–275″, where both catalogues are most complete.
    • It is high by 11 % (3.9σ, Poisson errors only) for 250–300″ as a whole.
    • The ratio steps down from 13.2 to 11.4 between the two halves of that annulus, a 2.6σ change. This coincides with HST losing F625W at 275–300″. The HST-alone ratio is flat across the step, so the step is probably not in the luminosity function.
  • Against the luminosity-function estimate, the fit is high by 10–15 %.
    • The HST-alone ratio divided by Gaia's completeness predicts a raw ratio of about 12.3, against the fitted 13.5–13.7.
    • The Gaia counts are fitted beyond 300″. If Gaia is more complete there than at 250–300″, as its rising N(G<17)/N(G<16) (1.75 at 250–275″, 1.87 at 275–300″) suggests, the expected raw ratio is lower still.
    • This estimate rests on two assumptions: the F625W − G offset holds at G ≈ 17, and the missing Gaia stars are a magnitude-blind subset.
  • What it implies for the model. With one stellar profile and the measured ratio, the current fits would predict roughly 5–15 % more G < 17 stars in the Gaia region than observed, relative to the HST region. Put another way, the fitted profile falls slightly too slowly between the two regions. The fits have no data at 250–300″, so this comparison relies on the model profile being smooth across the gap.
  • Precision is set by the catalogue edges. Only one 50″ annulus is usable, and Gaia completeness beyond 350″ cannot be checked against HST. This is a 5–15 % tension, not a firm offset. The completeness-corrected version below and the Large Programme fields put it at 13–15 %.

docs.title: Completeness-corrected ratio
docs.text:
(a) Completeness measured in each sample's own magnitude range.

  • Gaia, cG (solid blue): the fraction of oMEGACat stars with F625W < 16.83 (the HST equivalent of G < 17) that have a Gaia counterpart. The 0.06″ and 0.10″ match tolerances give the same values.
  • Dotted: cG in three magnitude slices.
  • HST, cH (red): the fraction of stars with F814W < 18.55 that have a measured F625W. Here 18.55 is the F814W equivalent of F625W = 19, using the median colour at 18.5 < F625W < 19.

(b) Ratio for complete samples.

  • Black: [NH19/cH] / [(NG17 − field)/cG].
  • Green: the HST-only ratio.
  • Purple band: the fitted aHST/aGaia, converted to complete samples.
  • Grey band: the inverse-variance mean of the corrected points at 150–275″.

Script: bin/check_count_ratio_corrected.py.

Completeness.

  • Gaia completeness depends strongly on magnitude.
    • At 250–300″ the G < 17 sample is 0.89 complete overall: 0.95 for F625W < 15.5, but only 0.77 just above the limit.
    • The bright-star value of 0.91–0.92 used above therefore overstated it.
  • HST F625W < 19 is complete. cH is 0.96–1.00 at every radius from 2 to 350″, with a count-weighted 0.990 over 2–250″.
    • The lower "F625W measured" fraction in the first plot (0.90 at 50–100″) comes from faint stars without F625W, not from stars brighter than F625W = 19.
    • So the HST count product does not carry the radial incompleteness suggested there.

The corrected ratio.

  • It is flat. From 10 to 275″ it is 10.5–11.9, wherever cG > 0.1, and it agrees with the HST-only ratio in every annulus. This confirms that the completeness estimates account for the inward climb of the raw ratio.
  • Mean. The mean at 150–275″ is 11.42 ± 0.23.
  • Edge annuli.
    • The 275–300″ point is low (10.1 ± 0.4). Beyond 300″ the corrected ratio falls to 6.9 and 2.4, although cH stays near 1 there.
    • The HST-only ratio does not fall, so this is a mismatch of area at the mosaic edge, not a change in the luminosity function. The edge cells are only partly covered by HST but are counted as fully covered for both catalogues (the likely explanation, not tested).
    • These points are excluded from the mean.

Comparison with the fit.

  • Converting the fitted ratio. The fitted aHST/aGaia contains each product's own completeness. It becomes a complete-sample ratio as fitted × cG,out / cH,in.
    • cH,in = 0.990.
    • cG,out is Gaia's completeness over the fitted 300–2400″. It cannot be measured against HST, so it is taken between 0.886 (the 250–300″ value) and 1.
    • This gives 12.3–13.9 for the no-BH fit. The black-hole fits are lower by at most 0.2.
  • Result. Against the measured 11.42 ± 0.23, the fitted ratio is 8–22 % too high. Even at the lower end of the band (Gaia completeness 0.886 beyond 300″) the difference is 3.7σ (Poisson errors only); the Large Programme section below gives the most likely value.
  • What it implies.
    • With one stellar profile, the fits put 8–22 % too many G < 17 stars in the Gaia region compared with the HST region.
    • The free aGaia hides this by scaling the Gaia counts down.
    • The remaining assumptions: the model profile is smooth across 250–300″, and the missing Gaia stars do not depend on position within each annulus.
  • Gaia completeness beyond 350″ is measured with further HST fields; see the next section. (An earlier reading of the oMEGACat data alone, a constant 0.9 "floor", is withdrawn.)

docs.title: Gaia completeness from the HST Large Programme fields (2026-10-16)
docs.text:
Gaia completeness of the G < 17 count sample against radius. Each point is the fraction of HST stars brighter than the HST equivalent of G = 17 that are present in the Vasiliev & Baumgardt (2021) catalogue used for the Gaia count product.

  • HST equivalent of G = 17: F606W = 17.03–17.09 (field-dependent median F606W − G), or F625W = 16.83 for oMEGACat.
  • Match: within 0.1″, after removing each field's epoch offset.
  • Grey lines: the Gaia count-product bins.
  • Black bars: the Large Programme fields combined, per bin with at least 10 stars.
  • Error bars: binomial; where every star is found, the 68 % lower limit.

Script: bin/check_gaia_completeness_lp.py. Numbers: results/plot_data/gaia_completeness_lp.json.

HST data. The HST Large Programme on ω Cen (GO-14118+14662, PI Bedin) has five external fields with public catalogues:

Field Radius Reference F5 224–435″ Scalco, Bedin & Vesperini 2024, A&A 688, A180 F4 262–443″ same F2 + F3 593–850″ Scalco et al. 2021, MNRAS 505, 3549 F1 868–1101″ Scalco, Bedin & Vesperini 2024

They are held in $OCEN_CATALOGUES/omegacen_hst_lp. These fields are uncrowded for Gaia's purposes, and HST is complete there to far below F606W = 17.

Results (stars found / HST stars):

R Large Programme fields cG oMEGACat 250–300″ 205/234 0.876 ± 0.022 0.886 ± 0.008 300–350″ (Gaia bin 1) 286/311 0.920 ± 0.015 0.894 ± 0.017 350–400″ (bin 2) 216/224 0.964 ± 0.012 — 400–450″ (bin 3) 83/89 0.933 ± 0.027 — 600–700″ 72/74 0.973 ± 0.019 — 700–800″ 70/76 0.921 ± 0.031 — 800–1000″ 38/39 0.974 ± 0.025 — beyond 500″, all 191/200 0.955 ± 0.015 —
  • Completeness rises outwards and then levels off. It is 0.88 at 250–300″ and 0.91 in the first Gaia bin (300–350″; oMEGACat and the Large Programme combined, 590/651). From 350″ to 1100″ it is a constant 0.95 within the errors.
  • The level of about 0.95 is not crowding. About 5 % of the HST stars brighter than G = 17 are missing from the Gaia catalogue even at 600–1100″. That could be stars without a five-parameter EDR3 solution, or losses in the catalogue selection (not identified).
    • In F2 + F3 the brightest stars (F606W < 15.5) are found at only 0.91. This may come from spurious HST detections around saturated stars (not tested).
  • Effect on the Gaia count product.
    • Only the first bin (300–350″) is depleted relative to the rest, by 0.906 / 0.955 = 0.95, i.e. 5 %. A free aGaia cannot absorb that.
    • The constant level of 0.95 is absorbed by aGaia.
  • Expected amplitude ratio for the raw counts.
    • The count-weighted Gaia completeness of the product is ceff = 0.946. The weights are member counts per bin, with cG = 0.906, 0.964, 0.933 in bins 1–3 and 0.955 beyond.
    • This gives aHST/aGaia = 11.42 × 0.990 / 0.946 = 11.95 ± 0.3.
    • The fits give 13.5–13.7, which is 13–15 % too high.

Change to the count likelihood (implemented 2026-10-16, commit 30bdcb3). It is used in the DF refit and in the count-based tracer of the Jeans twin. The code is kinematics/counts.py (CountProfile.completeness, CountTie, tied_compare), and the products are built by bin/build_count_completeness.py. The Gaia completeness beyond 350″ is 0.955, the Large Programme fields combined.

  1. Multiply the model Gaia counts in each bin by the measured cG: 0.906 in bin 1 (300–350″) and 0.955 (the Large Programme fields combined) from 350″ out, as stored in ocen_counts_gaia_g17_c.json. Equivalently, divide the data by it.
  2. Tie the amplitude: aGaia × cG(R) = aHST × 0.990 / 11.42, i.e. the ratio for complete samples, with its 2 % error carried as a Gaussian prior.
  3. aHST and the uniform field density b stay free. The field term counts the non-member Milky Way stars in the Gaia counts, and is unrelated to the cluster's luminosity function.

  • systemic PM (−3.250, −6.746) ± 0.022 mas/yr: Vasiliev & Baumgardt 2021, Table A1 (the earlier (−3.257, −6.730), labelled with that paper, matched no source);
  • v_los 232.7 ± 0.2 km/s: Baumgardt & Hilker 2018;
  • distance 5.43 ± 0.05 kpc: Baumgardt & Vasiliev 2021.

docs.title: M1. Present-day mass function and mass per counted star (M/N19)
docs.text:
• Inputs.
  • oMEGACat catalog_and_selections.fits: unflagged stars with F625W and F814W in zones 10–30–60–100–175–250″, with a common fit limit F625W < 21.0.
  • MIST v1.2 bolometric-correction tables, through minimint 0.5.1. HST_ACSWF.txz and HST_WFC3.txz were downloaded from waps.cfa.harvard.edu/MIST/BC_tables/v1/ and prepared into the prefix $OCEN_ISOCHRONES/minimint_hst/. That directory exists (241 MB; 70 filter files plus symlinks to the base grid). See the project journal.
  • Builder. bin/build_mass_function.py:
  • isochrone minimint.Interpolator(["ACS_WFC_F625W", "ACS_WFC_F814W"]) at line 82;
  • 12.5 Gyr, D = 5.43 kpc, E(B−V) = 0.12;
  • [Fe/H] from the ridge-line fit (adopted −1.20) or forced to --feh -1.53.
  • Products.
  • results/mass_function/mass_function_20260923.json (9,262 B).
  • results/mass_function/mass_function_feh153_20260923.json (9,275 B).
  • Keys: age_gyr, feh_adopted, ridge_fits, dm0, a625/a814, m_turnoff, zones and others.
  • Plot: plots/mass_function_*.png.
  • Result (the project journal). M/N19 = 8.4–9.5 M☉ per star in the kinematically dominant zones.
  • Use. An external prior. bin/run_mass_per_star_scan.sh pins the HST count amplitude with --mass-per-star ocen_counts_hst_f625w19=M for M = 7–12, writing results/df/mpsscan_*, mpsmock_* and related plots. It is not part of the baseline.

docs.title: Known gaps and inconsistencies
docs.text:
Found in the 2026-10-13 audit and updated on 2026-10-17. Each item is open unless marked otherwise.

  1. Scans still on the old (schema-1) count products. In progress.
  2. dftwo_counts_20260923, rho20scan_*, mpsscan_* and the 2026-09-23 mocks used schema-1 counts (star-weighted bin average, biased; see counts.py). Their frozen inputs still replay exactly; the old products are kept as *_schema1_20260923.*.
  3. The canonical ocen_counts_*.json are schema 2 since commit 1af8c33. The base model was refitted with them on 2026-10-13 (results/df/dftwo_counts_area_20261013, the reference fit), and again with completeness-corrected, tied counts on 2026-10-16 (results/df/dftie_restart_20261016).
  4. The halo test was redone with the tied counts (results/df/dftie_halo_20261016: the halo goes to zero). The rho20scan_* profile, the mpsscan_* mass-per-star scan and the mocks have not been rerun.
  5. Docstring and metadata drift.
  6. Fixed 2026-10-13: the bin/build_count_profiles.py docstring described the old quantile nodes.
  7. selection/field_template.py:107 writes "parallax_over_error_max": 5 into the product's cuts metadata, but no parallax cut is applied (parallax_cut: none). The metadata is misleading.
  8. likelihood.py:251 _edr3_ours admits that its note string describes an obsolete construction.
  9. Stale provenance records.
  10. The VB21 zip is read from $OCEN_CATALOGUES/vasiliev_baumgardt_2021_clusters.zip (manifest message "canonical store"). provenance/manifest.json and checksums.txt still keep a stale row for vasiliev2021_gc_members/clusters.zip at data/raw/vasiliev2021_gc_members/, which is empty.
  11. The manifest also keeps an obsolete kuzma2026_members.* row with status manual and exists=false, next to the real kuzma2026_members.txt entry.
  12. data/raw/baumgardt_gc_catalogue/ is empty because the file is referenced from CAT, which is intended.
  13. The T3 product's ocen_raw.manifest says unregistered, because it was built before the manifest entry existed.
  14. Registry incomplete.
  15. provenance/datasets.yaml omegacat_vi_kinematics has files: [], although 22 files are downloaded and md5-verified in the manifest.
  16. datasets.yaml omits the following:
    • STREAMFINDER 2021 and 2024, HST LP (all in configs/data.yaml only).
    • Tango Zenodo 4300977, gc_catalog_full.fits, Gaia XP/Andrae pulls.
    • Hunter, Portail, McMillan and MWPotential2014_mod potentials; DB98; GSE contours.

  19. S5 XP pulls.
  20. The S1 MRT→FITS conversion, which has no checksum for the FITS.
  21. External path dependencies outside the repository and CAT.
  22. Fixed: the VB21 zip is now in CAT.
  23. Fixed: the oCen_bar potentials and GSE contours under OB are reached through one convention, $OCEN_BAR_DIR (streams/restricted.py:37, tails/bar_migration.py:25).
  24. McMillan17 from the installed AGAMA package, so results depend on the AGAMA version.
  25. Inconsistent systemic values across modules. Resolved 2026-10-16.
  26. cluster.py is now the single reference for centre, systemic PM, v_los and distance, with published sources (see cluster data); about 110 typed-in copies in 47 files import it, and tests/test_cluster_reference.py bans new ones.
  27. Products built before that date keep the values they were built with (e.g. the K8 template frame, (−3.2514, −6.7444) from K6, v_los 232.6).
  28. Selection inconsistencies within the light and tracer chain.
  29. L2 (Jeans tracer and K4 depth term) uses oMEGACat selection_hq_f625w star counts inside 25″.
  30. C1 (DF reference fit) deliberately avoids that flag as 12–15 % radially incomplete.
  31. K10 hst_quality uses a flag that contains a CMD cut (project journal, 2026-10-08; flagged and not changed).
  32. Unverified references (per datasets.yaml or the project journal):
  33. Trager 1995 ADS link (verified: false).
  34. Baumgardt+2019 DOI (verified: false).
  35. Baumgardt GC database version.
  36. Kuzma+2021 (registered, no data, verified: false).
  37. Origins of the Portail17 and MWPotential2014_mod .ini files.
  38. GSE contours.
  39. The meaning of the VB21 profile undocumented_col12.
  40. Resolved 2026-10-17: Hunter+2024 (2024A&A...692A.216H) and Andrae+2023 (2023ApJS..267....8A), from docs/kb/literature.json.
  41. Registered or present but unused.

    • S3 STREAMFINDER 2021.

docs.title: Current: action-based DF models
docs.text:
Model What it adds to the base model Purpose Status Base no-DM model — Reference DF fit until 2026-10-16; parent of the black-hole fits Refitted 2026-10-13 with the corrected count likelihood; free count amplitudes, no completeness. Objective 280.7, χ²_kin 156.4 Tied, completeness-corrected DF refit per-bin count completeness; HST/Gaia amplitude ratio tied to the measured 11.42 ± 0.23 Reference DF fit (used for the dark-matter fits) Fitted 2026-10-16. Objective 295.77, χ²_kin 159.4; best fit (ML) M_rem 2.00×10⁵ M☉ Jeans comparison model, J-Trager spherical Jeans, fixed MGE light tracer (Trager+1995), turnover anisotropy, free black hole Earlier best model; tests a central black hole χ²_kin 190.0 (ML); M_BH 4.25 (3.92–4.58)×10⁴ M☉ (posterior median, 16–84 %) Jeans twin, J-counts as J-Trager, tracer an MGE of the completeness-corrected star counts (tied ratio) Tests the tracer dependence χ²_kin 152.2 (ML), below the DF's 156.4; M_BH 3.67 (3.30–4.02)×10⁴ M☉ (posterior median) DF + central black hole exact point mass M_BH = 8,200 or 4×10⁴ M☉ (fixed) in the DF potential Is a central black hole compatible with the DF fit? Objective 275.2 / 279.7 (base 280.7); 4×10⁴ over-predicts central counts. Free amplitudes, no completeness: not refitted with the tied counts. Cusp-depletion term proposed, not adopted Free cored halo gNFW halo with γ = 0, free \(\rho_{20}\) and \(r_s\) Do the data want extended dark matter? Free fit goes to \(\rho_{20}=0\): 2026-09-23 (old counts) and again with the tied counts (2026-10-16, results/df/dftie_halo_20261016; dark-matter fits) \(\rho_{20}\) profile \(\rho_{20}\) fixed at 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 M☉ pc⁻³, all else refitted How much DM is allowed at fixed fit quality Δ objective +0.5 … +10.6; a sensitivity curve, not a limit (mocks scatter by ±0.7) Mass-per-star scan HST count amplitude pinned at 8–12 M☉ per F625W < 19 star, free halo How the star/dark split depends on the assumed stellar mass \(\rho_{20}\) ≈ 2–4 at the photometric 8–9, 0 at the dynamical 10.7

Main results, figures and mock tests: DF observed-fit write-up (LaTeX). The \(\rho_{20}\) profile and the mass-per-star scan above use the count products from before the 2026-10-13 fix and have not been rerun; the free cored halo has been rerun with the tied counts.

Which DF fit is the reference: the tied, completeness-corrected refit (2026-10-16), on which the dark-matter fits are built; it changes the predictions of the 2026-10-13 base fit by a few per cent but moves M_rem by −27 %. The black-hole fits and most figures on the base-model page still use the 2026-10-13 fit.

docs.title: Parameters of each model
docs.text:
The base model has 10 free parameters (7 stellar, 2 remnant, the distance) and 3 profiled count nuisances. The dark-matter variants add a halo; the Jeans model has its own 10 parameters.

Model Parameters beyond the base model Range Fixed Free cored halo \(\rho_{20}\) (DM density at 20 pc), \(r_s\) (scale) 0–10 M☉ pc⁻³; 5–150 pc, log \(\gamma=0\) (core), taper \(r_t=1\) kpc \(\rho_{20}\) profile \(r_s\) 5–150 pc, log \(\rho_{20}\) = 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 Mass-per-star scan \(\rho_{20}\), \(r_s\) as the free halo HST count amplitude pinned: 8–12 M☉ per counted star

Halo density: \(\rho(r)=\rho_{20}\,(r/20\,{\rm pc})^{-\gamma}\,[(1+r/r_s)/(1+20/r_s)]^{\gamma-3}\,e^{-(r^2-20^2)/r_t^2}\).

What the data constrain. Twelve mocks drawn from the base model recover the total mass to ±3% at 20 pc and ±5% over 2–40 pc, but the recovered \(\rho_{20}\) scatters by 0.5–0.9 M☉ pc⁻³. The leading degeneracy is stellar mass against dark mass (remnants plus halo) through the count amplitude. Pinning the mass per counted star removes it but needs that number to ~3%; the photometric mass function gives 8.3–9.8 M☉ per star against the dynamical 10.7.

Implementation and history.

  • Regularized DF implementation: the DF family, numerics and tests.
  • Anisotropy diagnostics: why the model needs two anisotropy transitions (inner data want radial, outer data tangential anisotropy).
  • Observed-data flexibility: the one-transition DF fails (χ²/N ≈ 4.8).
  • Compact DF proposal (PDF), compact DF recovery, frequency-mapper diagnostic.
  • Earlier mixture DF (superseded): AGAMA DF models, capacity challenge, mass recovery.
  • DF model literature review.
  • Next steps under discussion: Codex review, 2026-10-13 (multi-mass stellar populations, remnant treatment).

Dark matter (2026-10-16). All three reference models were refitted with a dark-matter halo: J-Trager and J-counts each with an NFW and a cored halo, and the tied DF with a cored halo. None prefers one, as the dark-matter fits show.

docs.title: Base model: two-transition DF, no dark matter
docs.text:
The DF model of the cluster mass distribution, in two fits: the 2026-10-13 base fit (free count amplitudes, below) and the tied, completeness-corrected refit of 2026-10-16. The tied refit is the reference DF fit from 2026-10-16 on; the dark-matter fits are built on it. The base fit is the parent of the fixed-black-hole fits on DF + central black hole.

Status (2026-10-13)

Refitted on 2026-10-13 with the corrected (area-weighted) count likelihood: results/df/dftwo_counts_area_20261013, best job observed_no_halo_start3. The fit is numerically validated but fails its own data-fit gate. It supersedes the 2026-09-23 fit (results/df/dftwo_counts_20260923), whose star-weighted count averages were biased; parameters moved by ≤ 4% and the mass per counted star by −1.8%.

Status (2026-10-16)

Superseded as the reference DF fit by the tied, completeness-corrected refit (results/df/dftie_restart_20261016, objective 295.77). Its predictions differ from this fit by a few per cent; M_rem falls by 27 %. This fit stays the parent of the black-hole fits, which have not been redone with the tied counts.

docs.title: Stellar DF
docs.text:
The regularized exponential action DF (contour construction of Binney 2026, MNRAS 549, stag854, doi:10.1093/mnras/stag854), rebuilt at every iteration and iterated to self-consistency in the total potential (stars + remnants):

\[ f(\mathbf J)=A\,\exp\!\left[-\left(L_c/J_0\right)^{\alpha}\right], \qquad q=J_r+L . \]

The contour label \(L_c\) follows the spherical frequency ratio, biased by the anisotropy function \(b(q)\): \(b>0\) favours radial orbits, \(b<0\) tangential ones. Two transitions:

\[ b(q)=b_{\rm out}\,s(q;J_a)+\left(b_{\rm outer}-b_{\rm out}\right)s(q;J_{\rm outer}), \qquad s(q;J)=\frac{q^2}{q^2+J^2}. \]

The core is isotropic (\(b\to0\) as \(q\to0\)); the model is radially anisotropic at intermediate radii and tangential outside.

Parameter Meaning Range Best fit \(J_0\) envelope scale (pc km/s) 30–800, log 56.0 \(\alpha\) envelope sharpness 0.6–3 0.80 \(b_{\rm out}\) intermediate anisotropy −2 to 2 +0.77 (radial) \(J_a\) first transition (pc km/s) 5–500, log 65.5 \(b_{\rm outer}\) outer anisotropy −4 to 2 −0.33 (tangential) \(J_{\rm outer}\) second transition (pc km/s) 2–100 × \(J_a\) 312

docs.title: How the stellar mass is determined
docs.text:
• Seven stellar parameters: the mass normalisation \(M_\star\) and the six DF parameters (\(J_0\), \(\alpha\), \(b_{\rm out}\), \(J_a\), \(b_{\rm outer}\), \(J_{\rm outer}\)). The stellar density is not an input: it is computed from \(f(\mathbf J)\) in the total potential, so the envelope and the anisotropy parameters together set its shape.
  • The star counts constrain the shape only. Their amplitude (counted stars per unit model surface density) is a nuisance parameter, profiled analytically at every evaluation; the counts say where the stars are, not how much mass they carry.
  • \(M_\star\) is set by the kinematics, jointly with the remnants. It is not taken from photometry. The mass per counted star (10.48 M☉ per F625W < 19 star) is therefore an output of the fit.
  • The only place \(M_\star\) is fixed externally is the mass-per-star scan, where the count amplitude is held at a value from the photometric mass function instead of being profiled.
  • Mass-to-light ratio. With L_V = 1.16×10⁶ L☉ (Harris catalogue V = 3.68 and E(B−V) = 0.12, at the fitted 5.356 kpc), \(M_\star/L_V = 2.6\) and \(M_{\rm tot}/L_V = 2.8\).

docs.title: Remnant component
docs.text:
\[ \rho_{\rm rem}(r)=\frac{3M_{\rm rem}}{4\pi a_{\rm rem}^3} \left(1+\frac{r^2}{a_{\rm rem}^2}\right)^{-5/2} \]

It stands for all mass that does not follow the counted light: neutron stars and stellar-mass black holes, any mass-segregated white dwarfs and heavy stars, and part of the effect of a central black hole. At the best fit it holds 8% of the total mass, has a half-mass radius of \(1.305\,a_{\rm rem}=2.8\) pc, and dominates the mass inside ~1.5 pc (60% inside 1 pc).

Comparison with the literature: published fits find 1.35–2.65×10⁵ M☉ in a central non-luminous component; Bañares-Hernández+2025 fit the same Plummer form and get 2.65×10⁵ M☉ with a 1.88 pc scale. Details: Remnant mass and spatial scale.

Is this remnant mass physically sensible? It is 8.4% of the total and 0.09 of the stellar mass, inside the IMF budget for remnants heavier than the tracer stars (8.7–11.8% with all black holes retained): Remnant mass and the stellar population.

docs.title: Distance, geometry, rotation
docs.text:
• Distance free in 4.8–6.0 kpc with a Gaussian prior \(N(5.43, 0.05)\) kpc; best fit 5.356 kpc (1.5σ low).
  • Spherical and non-rotating. The published rotation is removed at the moment level, \(\sigma^2_{\rm pred}=\langle v^2\rangle_{\rm DF}-v^2_{\rm rot}\); a negative result is rejected, never floored.

The HST count residuals remain structured: the data lie below the model near 1 pc and in the outermost HST bin (~6 pc), with deviance residuals of about −4, and above it at 3–4 pc (+4.6).

The fitted ratio is 13–15 % higher than expected (13.5–13.7 against 11.95 ± 0.3).

docs.title: Comparison with the Jeans model (dashed curves)
docs.text:
Full description, figures and posterior: Jeans comparison model.

The dashed curves are the best rung-2 spherical Jeans fit without dark matter (results/fits/rung2_K1_turnover, J-Trager), the best no-DM model of the earlier Jeans ladder. Both models are fitted to the same 89-bin kinematic snapshot, so their kinematic χ² compare directly; the Jeans fit uses a fixed light profile (an MGE of the Trager+1995 profile, 1995AJ....109..218T, joined to HST star counts) instead of the Poisson star counts.

Jeans (rung 2, no DM) DF base model Stellar tracer and mass MGE light profile, mass-to-light free self-consistent action DF Free stellar parameters \(M_\star\) only (density shape fixed by the light) \(M_\star\) and six DF parameters (shape fitted to the counts) Anisotropy turnover β(r): β₀ = −0.50 (centre) → +0.20 → −0.98 (outside) isotropic core → +0.15 near 8 pc → −0.53 at 100 pc Central black hole 4.41×10⁴ M☉ (ML); 4.25 (3.92–4.58)×10⁴ (median, 16–84%) none \(M_\star\) 2.37×10⁶ M☉ (ML) 3.00×10⁶ M☉ (best fit) Remnants (Plummer) 7.7×10⁵ M☉, a = 5.7 pc (ML) 2.7×10⁵ M☉, a = 2.2 pc (best fit) Total mass, M★ + Mrem + MBH 3.18×10⁶ M☉ (ML); 3.24×10⁶ (median) 3.27×10⁶ M☉ (best fit) \(M_\star/L_V\), \(M_{\rm tot}/L_V\) 2.0, 2.7 (ML); 2.3, 2.8 (median) 2.6, 2.8 Distance 5.34 kpc 5.36 kpc χ² (per bin) Jeans DF HST PM radial (21) 61.8 (2.94) 42.6 (2.03) HST PM tangential (21) 36.6 (1.74) 39.8 (1.89) MUSE LOS (29) 51.7 (1.78) 38.1 (1.31) Gaia PM radial (9) 16.9 (1.88) 14.4 (1.60) Gaia PM tangential (9) 23.0 (2.56) 21.5 (2.39) Total (89) 190.0 156.4
  • The DF fits better than J-Trager overall (Δχ² = 34) and in every dataset except the HST tangential proper motions. The Jeans twin with the star-count tracer (J-counts) reaches χ² = 152.2, below the DF's 156.4 (and the tied refit's 159.4).
  • The Jeans model follows the central rise of the HST proper-motion dispersions inside 0.3 pc (~11″), which the DF, with an isotropic core and no black hole, stays below by 1.5–2.4σ in several bins: χ² = 7.3 (Jeans) against 21.5 (DF) for those 10 bins. This is where the black hole matters.
  • It pays for this at intermediate radii: at 2–20 pc (36 bins of HST, MUSE and Gaia) χ² = 122.2 (Jeans) against 77.8 (DF), mostly in the HST radial proper motions (40.2 against 20.2) and the MUSE line-of-sight dispersions (30.9 against 18.7).
  • The black hole is tied to an imposed anisotropy. A cored stellar density around a point mass needs β₀ ≤ −½ for any non-negative DF; the prior enforces it and the fit sits at the bound (β₀ = −0.503). Even so, under the standard separable construction a non-negative DF fails to exist at 0.02–0.18 pc, where the black hole dominates (89.7% of posterior draws fail; no failure outside ~0.2 pc; a non-separable DF is not excluded; DF consistency audit). The DF base model is non-negative by construction.
  • Both put about the same total mass in the cluster (3.2–3.3×10⁶ M☉) but divide it differently: the Jeans fit has 20% less stellar mass and nearly three times more remnant mass, spread over a 2.5× larger scale. This is the same stars-versus-dark-mass degeneracy seen within the DF fits.
  • Why \(M_\star\) differs by 11% at the same total mass. In neither model is the stellar mass fixed by the light or the counts; it is the normalisation the kinematics leave after the remnants (and, for Jeans, the black hole and the imposed central anisotropy) take their share. The remnant mass is close to the total minus \(M_\star\), so with remnants at 8–17% of the total, a 1% change in \(M_\star\) moves \(M_{\rm rem}\) by ~10%.
  • A central black hole in the DF (DF + central black hole, 2026-10-15, fixed masses): 8,200 M☉ lowers the objective by 5.5; 4×10⁴ M☉ lowers χ²_kin by 12 but loses 15 in the HST counts (objective −1.0). The differences are not calibrated with mocks. Whether the inner rise needs a black hole, radially biased central orbits or mass segregation is not settled.

docs.title: Refit with completeness-corrected counts and tied amplitudes (2026-10-16)
docs.text:
This refit uses the same model, data and settings, with two changes to the count likelihood:

  • Per-bin detection completeness. HST 0.96–0.995; Gaia 0.906 in its first bin and 0.955 beyond.
  • A tied amplitude ratio. aHST/aGaia for complete samples has a prior N(11.42, 0.23), from the measured ratio.

The fit was seeded from the base best fit and then restarted from its own best point; the restart changed the objective by less than 0.001. Runs: results/df/dftie_seed_20261016 and results/df/dftie_restart_20261016.

Data with both models, and residuals. Blue: the base fit (free amplitudes). Orange: the tied refit. Dashed: the Jeans model J-Trager.

Interpretation

  • The predictions change by a few per cent at most. The kinematic curves overlap. With the ratio tied, the Gaia counts at 15–30 pc lie 3–4σ above the model, i.e. 3–4 % in a bin of about 1,000 stars. The outermost HST bin improves.
  • The parameters move much more. Mrem drops by 27 % and the anisotropy changes, while the total mass stays the same. These parameters are therefore only weakly fixed by the data: a few per cent in the predictions trades against tens of per cent in them.
  • The DF's outer envelope may be too rigid (untested). One smooth profile does fit both count sets with the measured ratio: the MGE of the Jeans twin has Gaia deviance 13.5 over 12 bins, against 45.9 for the tied DF refit.

docs.title: What has been tested
docs.text:
• Convergence: 4 of 6 starts valid (2 Latin starts infeasible), all four reach the same minimum (objectives within 0.01); no parameter at a bound.
  • Numerics: grid refinement shifts predictions by 0.0005σ; direct projection checks agree to ≤ 5×10⁻⁴ in Σ, LOS, PM_R and PM_T.
  • Estimator recovery (2026-09-23 fit, old count likelihood): 12 mocks drawn from this model with published kinematic noise and Poisson counts recover the total mass to ±3% at 20 pc and ±5% over 2–40 pc, \(M_\star\) to ±6%, \(M_{\rm rem}\) to ±23%.

Not yet tested: mocks whose truth breaks the model's own assumptions (mass segregation, rotation, another remnant shape); calibration of the error bars.

docs.title: Built-in assumptions
docs.text:
1. Mass follows light: one stellar DF is both tracer and mass.
  2. Isotropic core.
  3. One remnant component with a fixed Plummer shape.
  4. No central black hole.
  5. Spherical; rotation subtracted from published curves.
  6. Published error bars taken as they are.

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
source <venv>/bin/activate
export PYTHONPATH=src
python bin/run_compact_df_recovery.py prepare-real --out results/df/<new_label> \
  --two-transition --branches no_halo \
  --counts ocen_counts_hst_f625w19,ocen_counts_gaia_g17 \
  --free-distance 4.8:6.0 --distance-prior 5.43:0.05 \
  --bound stellar.J0=30:800 --bound stellar.J_a=5:500 --bound stellar.b_out=-2:2 \
  --hand-starts 2 --n-starts 4 --probe-workers 5
python bin/run_compact_df_recovery.py run --out results/df/<new_label> --workers 2 --max-calls 600

Each run uses 2 jobs × (5 probe workers + 1) = 12 cores and took ~30 min in September. The batch freezes its source, configuration and inputs; a run directory is never reused.

Code: src/ocen_dm/kinematics/regularized_df.py (DF, remnants, halo), df_fit.py (joint problem), counts.py (count likelihood), compact_recovery.py (mocks, residuals), bin/run_compact_df_recovery.py (driver).

docs.title: Central black hole: cusp depletion (proposal)
docs.text:
Status: proposal, not adopted

Proposed 2026-10-15. No decision has been taken: no code for the depletion term exists and no fits with it have been run. The model in use is unchanged. This page records the evidence, the proposal, its costs and the open questions so the decision can be taken later.

docs.title: In short
docs.text:
• Adding a central point mass (black hole) to our stellar DF forces an isotropic stellar cusp, ρ ∝ r−3/2, around it. This follows from a DF that stays finite at small actions.
  • With MBH = 4×104 M⊙ the model reproduces the central rise of the proper-motion and line-of-sight dispersions. But it over-predicts the HST star counts at 2–13″ (0.05–0.35 pc), where the counts are flat.
  • That excess is not explained by crowding or by the choice of centre (tests below). The published completeness-corrected counts are also flat: projected slope 0.00 ± 0.07 inside 15″.
  • Proposal: a one-parameter depletion of the most bound orbits, which lets the model have a shallower cusp around the black hole.

docs.title: Fits with a fixed central point mass
docs.text:
The black-hole mass was fixed. Everything else was refitted: stellar mass, remnant mass and scale, distance, DF shape. Each fit used one start, seeded from the no-BH best fit, and was restarted from its own best point, changing the objective by less than 0.004. Otherwise the settings were those of the 2026-10-13 base fit: free count amplitudes and raw counts without the completeness correction. These fits have not been redone with the tied, completeness-corrected counts of the reference DF refit.

Model Objective χ²kin (89 bins) HST counts deviance (20 bins) Gaia counts deviance (12 bins) M★ Mrem arem (pc) Total mass No BH (base) 280.7 156.4 96.9 25.2 3.00×10⁶ 2.73×10⁵ 2.18 3.27×10⁶ BH 8,200 M⊙ 275.2 152.7 95.9 24.5 2.96×10⁶ 2.89×10⁵ 2.43 3.26×10⁶ BH 4×10⁴ M⊙ 279.7 144.5 112.0 21.6 2.67×10⁶ 5.04×10⁵ 4.05 3.21×10⁶
  • Columns. The objective is χ²kin plus the two Poisson count deviances plus the distance-prior term (2.2, 2.3 and 1.7); for the base fit 156.4 + 96.9 + 25.2 + 2.2 = 280.7. Lower is better. Masses are best-fit (maximum-likelihood) values in M⊙. The total mass is M★ + Mrem + MBH; there is no dark-matter halo in these fits.
  • Not a measurement. None of the three passes the data-fit gate (χ² per bin ≈ 1.7), so the differences are not yet calibrated. That needs mocks with an injected black hole.
  • How the 4×10⁴ fit compensates. Less stellar mass, more remnant mass spread over a larger scale (its density at 0.3 pc is 0.30 of the base value), and a more radial inner DF.

The two count profiles do not join, by design: they are different selections in their own units. HST counts are oMEGACat stars with F625W < 19 at 2–250″; Gaia counts are stars with G < 17 at 300–2400″. The brighter Gaia limit counts fewer stars per unit stellar mass: the fitted amplitude ratio aHST/aGaia is 13.5–13.7 (free amplitudes, raw counts), against a measured 11.42 ± 0.23 for complete samples, i.e. 11.95 ± 0.3 expected for the raw counts (count-ratio check). So each profile has its own fitted count amplitude (aHST, aGaia), and the Gaia model also includes a uniform field of about 1.6 stars arcmin⁻². The model curves are the same stellar surface density scaled by each amplitude. The gap between 250″ and 300″ is a gap in coverage.

docs.title: The central HST counts
docs.text:
The HST counts are all oMEGACat stars with F625W < 19.

Check Result Crowding: oMEGACat magnitude-slice ratios (< 17, 17–18, 19–20 against 18–19) flat inside 10″ to 10–20 %; only F625W 20–21 may be 10–15 % low. This test cannot see losses common to all magnitudes Poisson: inner two bins (2–3.2″) observed 6, 12. No BH: expected 10.8, 17.5 (P = 0.09, 0.11). BH 4×10⁴: expected 14.1, 22.1 (P = 0.013, 0.014) Centre: 25 centres within ±2″ plus the oMEGACat VI kinematic centre the innermost "drop" is noise from the centre choice (innermost bin holds 3–16 stars). Over the 8 inner bins (2–13″), BH 4×10⁴ is worse than no BH at every centre: deviance +6 to +19, median +12. BH 8,200 cannot be told apart from no BH (−0.6 to +1.8) Literature Anderson & van der Marel 2010: completeness-corrected counts (> 80 % complete even at the centre) are flat, with a marginally lower centre. van der Marel & Anderson 2010: projected slope inside 15″ is 0.00 ± 0.07. oMEGACat publishes no artificial-star tests

Scripts: bin/check_hst_count_completeness.py, bin/check_count_centre.py.

docs.title: Expectations from simulations
docs.text:
• N-body-style models. González Prieto et al. 2025 grew black holes of 47,000–51,000 M⊙ in omega Cen models. The stars settle to a 3-D density slope γ ≈ 1.3, and the models predict a slightly brighter inner core than observed.
  • Projected slopes. Baumgardt, Makino & Hut 2005 find shallow projected slopes of bright stars, about −0.1 to −0.3, even with a black hole.
  • Our cusp is steeper than both. Our DF is forced to γ = 1.5 inside the black hole's sphere of influence: 0.07 pc for 8,200 M⊙, about 0.3 pc for 4×10⁴ M⊙.

docs.title: The proposal
docs.text:
Multiply the stellar DF by a depletion factor in the contour label Lc:

\[ D(L_c)=\frac{(L_c/J_c)^p}{1+(L_c/J_c)^p}, \]

renormalised, in both the DF and its normalisation integral, so that the stellar mass is unchanged.

  • One new free parameter, Jc, the depletion scale. With Jc = 0 the model is exactly the current one.
  • p is fixed per experiment. In an isotropic Kepler region the density goes as r−(3−p)/2 for p < 2, as r−1/2 log r for p = 2, and as r−1/2 for p > 2. The plan is p = 4 first (the shallowest cusp, r−1/2), then p = 1 and p = 0.4 (limiting slopes 1 and 1.3). p would be freed only if mocks show the data can separate it from Jc.
  • Why depletion in Lc, not in the total action. It keeps the existing energy-like contours and so does not change the DF's angular weighting (Codex review).
  • Physical motivation, if adopted. The central cusp has been depleted, for example by scouring or a cusp that has not regrown. The depletion term is a phenomenological stand-in, not a model of that process.

docs.title: Consequences and caveats
docs.text:
• Kinematics. In a black-hole-dominated power-law region σr² = GM/((γ+1) r). Depleting the cusp (γ from 1.5 to 0.5) raises the local dispersion by 5/3, while projection weakens the observed rise. Black-hole mass and depletion may trade off, in no fixed direction, so any result needs a profile in (MBH, Jc).
  • Scope of the depletion. It applies to the whole self-gravitating stellar DF, not only to the counted tracer. The count likelihood cannot represent a radial change of mass per counted star.
  • Remnants stay a fixed Plummer sphere (declared caveat). Stellar depletion and a remnant cusp should not both be freed in the first experiment. A concentrated-remnant alternative is a separate later test.
  • Numerical risks. Two need independent checks:
    • the near-escape velocity shell, which may dominate a strongly depleted centre;
    • the action guard, whose "can only remove mass" argument fails for a non-monotonic DF.

docs.title: Validation needed before any fit
docs.text:
1. Jc = 0 reproduces the current model exactly; configuration and optimizer round trips; positivity.
  2. Kepler density and pressure benchmarks for p < 2, p = 2 and p > 2.
  3. An independent escape-shell reference, and convergence of every count expectation and dispersion bin.
  4. The guard against exact actions across the depleted family; independent mass normalisation.
  5. Multiple starts at MBH = 0, 8,200 and 4×10⁴, and profiles in (MBH, Jc).
  6. Mocks with injected depleted and undepleted truths before any significance is quoted.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text:
• Code and validation (items 1–4): about half a day.
  • Fits: about 1–2 hours per black-hole mass on 6 cores. The first set (three masses, p = 4) takes about 4–6 hours; each further p value repeats that.
  • Mocks: extra, to be sized when needed.

docs.title: Alternatives that need no new parameter
docs.text:
• Keep the model and report the tension. This is a defensible result in its own right.
  • Fit only R > 3″ counts, as a sensitivity case only. It cannot remove a tension that extends to 13″.
  • Other forms, each with a different physical meaning: depletion in energy (equivalent to Lc in pure Kepler), a DF floor, a loss cone (suppresses low angular momentum and predicts tangential anisotropy), or a centrally concentrated remnant component.

docs.title: Decisions pending
docs.text:
1. Adopt the depletion term at all (or one of the alternatives)?
  2. If yes: run the validation, then the fits, and in which order?

docs.title: DF + central black hole
docs.text:
The base model with an exact central point mass added to the potential. The black-hole mass is fixed in each fit, at 8,200 M⊙ or 4×104 M⊙. Every other parameter is refitted. Fitted 2026-10-15, with the count likelihood of the 2026-10-13 base fit (free amplitudes, no completeness correction); not yet refitted with the tied, completeness-corrected counts of the current reference DF fit.

  • Why these two masses. 8,200 M⊙ is the robust lower limit from the fast stars (Häberle et al. 2024, Nature 631, 285; arXiv:2405.06015). 4×104 M⊙ is close to the masses preferred by that paper's acceleration and N-body analyses, and to our Jeans comparison models (posterior medians 4.25×104 with the Trager tracer, 3.67×104 with the star-count tracer).
  • Not a measurement. The black-hole mass is not free, none of the three models passes the data-fit gate, and the objective differences are not yet calibrated with mocks.
  • Next step, undecided. The cusp-depletion proposal records the tension with the central star counts found here and a possible model extension.

docs.title: What the black hole changes
docs.text:
• Potential. A Plummer sphere of zero scale radius, i.e. an exact point mass, is added to the stars and the fixed Plummer remnants. The stellar DF is solved self-consistently in the total potential, as in the base model.
  • Central stellar cusp. The DF stays finite at small actions, so around a point mass it produces an isotropic cusp ρ★ ∝ r−3/2. This sets in inside the sphere of influence: 0.07 pc for 8,200 M⊙ and about 0.3 pc for 4×104 M⊙. This is a property of the DF family, not a fitted result.
  • Numerics. Orbit frequencies and actions around the point mass use AGAMA, with exact quadratures substituted where AGAMA's spherical routines fail near a point mass. Those failures are NaN, unbound or wrongly sized orbits, mostly far outside the cluster. AGAMA's ordinary errors move the bin predictions by at most 0.01σ. Models without a black hole are unchanged (the base fit is reproduced exactly).

docs.title: Fit quality
docs.text:
The fit-quality numbers and the two figures below are from the seed fits (results/df/dfbh{8200,40000}_seed_20261015); the parameters above are from the restarts. The restarts changed the objective by less than 0.004.

Term Gate No BH 8,200 4×10⁴ χ²kin per bin (89 bins) ≤ 1.3 156.4 / 89 = 1.76 152.7 / 89 = 1.72 144.5 / 89 = 1.62 HST PM radial, per bin ≤ 2.0 2.03 1.93 1.60 HST PM tangential, per bin ≤ 2.0 1.89 1.83 1.86 MUSE LOS, per bin ≤ 2.0 1.31 1.29 1.22 Gaia PM radial, per bin ≤ 2.0 1.60 1.64 1.85 Gaia PM tangential, per bin ≤ 2.0 2.39 2.38 2.20 HST count deviance (20 bins) ≤ 2.0 per bin 96.9 (4.8) 95.9 (4.8) 112.0 (5.6) Gaia count deviance (12 bins) ≤ 2.0 per bin 25.2 (2.1) 24.5 (2.0) 21.6 (1.8) Distance prior term — 2.2 2.3 1.7 Total objective — 280.7 275.2 279.7
  • No model passes the data-fit gate. All three pass the numerical-validation gate, and no parameter sits at a bound.
  • 8,200 M⊙ improves every term slightly: the objective falls by 5.5.
  • 4×104 M⊙ fits the central kinematics better (χ²kin −12), mainly the HST radial proper motions. But it loses 15 on the HST counts, so the objective falls by only 1.0.
  • Convergence. Each BH fit is a single start from the no-BH best fit, restarted from its own best point; the restarts changed the objective by less than 0.004.

The two count profiles do not join, by design: they are different selections in their own units. HST counts are oMEGACat stars with F625W < 19 at 2–250″; Gaia counts are stars with G < 17 at 300–2400″. The brighter Gaia limit counts fewer stars per unit stellar mass: the fitted amplitude ratio aHST/aGaia is 13.5–13.7 in these fits (free amplitudes, raw counts), while the measured ratio is 11.42 ± 0.23 for complete samples, i.e. 11.95 ± 0.3 expected for the raw counts. Each profile has its own fitted count amplitude (aHST, aGaia), and the Gaia model also includes a uniform field of about 1.6 stars arcmin⁻². The model curves are the same stellar surface density scaled by each amplitude. The gap between 250″ and 300″ is a gap in coverage. Measurement: the count-ratio check. The fitted ratio is 13–15 % higher than expected.

What the data comparison shows:

  • Inside about 0.3 pc, only the 4×104 model rises in proper-motion dispersion, to about 0.85 mas/yr, and in LOS dispersion, to about 21 km/s. That matches the innermost HST and MUSE points, like the Jeans comparison model. The 8,200 model rises only in the innermost bin.
  • The same cusp over-predicts the HST star counts at 2–13″ (0.05–0.35 pc), where the counts are flat. That excess is not explained by crowding or by the choice of centre; see the checks on the proposal page.
  • Beyond about 1 pc, the three models cannot be told apart.

docs.title: M<sub>BH</sub> = 4×10<sup>4</sup> M<sub>⊙</sub>
docs.text:
• Panels and shading are as for the base model. The black hole appears in the enclosed-mass and circular-velocity panels. Shading marks radii outside the kinematic data (0.1–63 pc).
  • Inner rise. Inside about 0.1 pc the intrinsic dispersions and the stellar density rise inwards. That is the r−3/2 cusp, which lies mostly inside the innermost data bins.

docs.title: Data, likelihood and settings
docs.text:
• As the 2026-10-13 base fit. Same 89 kinematic bins, HST and Gaia count profiles (ocen_counts_hst_f625w19, ocen_counts_gaia_g17: raw counts, no completeness correction), free count amplitudes, and likelihood (base model: data and likelihood).
  • Not refitted with the tied counts. The 8,200 and 4×104 M⊙ fits have not been redone with the completeness-corrected counts and the tied amplitude ratio of the reference DF refit (objective 295.77 without a black hole); their objectives compare only with the base fit's 280.7.
  • Fit settings. Two-transition DF, no halo, free distance with the N(5.43, 0.05) kpc prior, --fix matter.M_bh, equilibrium tolerance 5×10⁻⁵.
  • Runs:
    • fits: results/df/dfbh{8200,40000}_seed_20261015;
    • restarts (the values above): results/df/dfbh{8200,40000}_restart_20261015;
    • figures: bin/plot_best_fit_performance.py, bin/plot_base_model_properties.py.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Fixed mass, single start. MBH is fixed, not fitted, and each mass has one start, so these are compatibility tests, not a black-hole mass measurement.
  • Imposed cusp. The central cusp comes from the DF family, not from the data. A depleted cusp (proposal) could change the preferred mass in either direction.
  • Fixed Plummer remnants. The remnants stay a fixed Plummer sphere, with no central concentration of heavy remnants.
  • Uncalibrated differences. Objective differences are not yet calibrated: χ² per bin is about 1.7 in all three models, so mocks with an injected black hole are needed before any significance is quoted.

docs.title: Dark-matter fits of the reference models
docs.text:
Each reference model is refitted with a dark-matter halo added, with all other ingredients unchanged (fits of 2026-10-16; J-Trager halo runs of 2026-09-21).

  • Jeans models. These are J-Trager (tracer: composite HST/Trager light profile) and J-counts (tracer: completeness-corrected HST + Gaia star counts with the tied amplitude ratio; twin model). Each is fitted with an NFW halo and with a cored halo.
  • DF model. This is the tied, completeness-corrected refit, fitted with a free cored halo.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Neither tracer needs dark matter.
    • The evidence changes by Δln Z = +0.1 and +1.2 (J-Trager) and +1.1 ± 0.6 and +0.5 ± 0.8 (J-counts) for NFW and cored halos.
    • The best-fit likelihood improves by at most 3.5 for 2 extra parameters.
  • The DF fit drives the halo to zero. All three starts end at ρ20 ≈ 0, and none beats the no-halo objective.
  • The halo the Jeans fits allow sits mostly outside the kinematic data.
    • Inside the outermost kinematic bin (63 pc), the dark-matter share of the mass is below about 10 %.
    • Inside the data the total mass is the same with and without a halo; the models differ only beyond it.
  • The small likelihood gain is spread over several datasets. For J-counts, Δχ² = −6.2 (NFW) and −7.0 (cored): the Gaia radial PMs give −2.5 and −2.6, almost all from the two outermost bins (beyond about 1,500″, the bins most exposed to tidal effects and escaping stars); the HST tangential PMs −3.2 and −2.3; MUSE −1.6 and −1.3 (breakdown).
  • The halo mass is not measured. MDM(<100 pc) spans more than a factor of 10 and trades against the stars and remnants.
  • The black-hole mass is unchanged by the halo: 3.6–3.7×10⁴ M⊙ with the count tracer, 4.3×10⁴ M⊙ with Trager.

docs.text:
The tied, completeness-corrected count likelihood was used, with three starts (2 at a time, 3 probe workers each, about 30 min). Run: results/df/dftie_halo_20261016.
